picks.d: Sammy's personal pick of the week, full stop. The legendary composer behind every Studio Ghibli score you've ever ugly-cried to — Totoro, Spirited Away, Princess Mononoke — conducts his own music live at Davies Symphony Hall. This is the kind of night you'll talk about for years. Grab whoever you love most and go.

picks.t: WNBA Finals Game 1 — Golden State Valkyries vs. Atlanta Dream
picks.d: History is happening right here. The Valkyries are in their first-ever WNBA Finals and Game 1 is at Chase Center — the energy in that building is going to be absolutely unreal. This is a watershed moment for Bay Area sports and you do not want to be watching from your couch.

picks.t: Neurosis — Two Nights at The Fillmore
picks.d: SF's own legendary metal titans return home after eight years away, playing two special nights at the Fillmore in support of their new album with Aaron Turner of Isis and Sumac joining the lineup. Kowloon Walled City opens Friday. If you know, you know — and if you don't, now is the time to find out.

picks.t: T-Pain & Ari Lennox at Golden Gate Park
picks.d: An outdoor concert in Robin Williams Meadow with T-Pain headlining and Ari Lennox opening — plus DJs Lady Ryan, Shellheart, and BBCAROLZ rounding out the day. It's a full Golden Gate Park hang with genuine star power. Grab your crew, a blanket, and snacks and make a whole afternoon of it.

picks.t: Public Works 16-Year Anniversary — Detroit Love w/ Carl Craig & Moodymann
picks.d: One of SF's most beloved venues throws a two-night birthday party and invites two of Detroit techno's all-time greats to headline. Carl Craig and Moodymann on the same night at full-capacity Public Works is an event that dance music fans will be talking about for a long time. Night Three on Saturday features QUEEN OUT x FAKE & GAY.

picks.t: Heavens to Betsy — Two Nights at Bottom of the Hill
picks.d: Both nights are already sold out, which tells you everything. Corin Tucker's foundational riot grrrl duo is a piece of feminist punk history and seeing them at Bottom of the Hill — one of SF's most intimate rooms — is the kind of show that just doesn't come around. Check resale and make it happen.

picks.t: Sara Bareilles — The Good Grief Tour
picks.d: Sara Bareilles returns to the road with her first album in seven years, the deeply personal Good Grief, and she's doing two nights at Bill Graham Civic with Celisse opening. Warm, honest, and genuinely great live — this is a show for anyone who's ever needed a song to get them through something hard.

Peaches is one of the most fearlessly original live performers on the planet and she's bringing her full theatrical chaos to Great American Music Hall as part of Psyched! Fest. SOLTERA, Sola Guinto, and Shifters!! open. If you've never seen her live, this is your moment — expect to leave changed.

picks.t: Exploratorium After Dark — Death and Life / La muerte y la vida
picks.d: The Exploratorium's adults-only After Dark series goes full Día de los Muertos this week, transforming the entire Pier 15 space into a late-night celebration of life, death, and everything in between. This is genuinely unlike any other night out in SF — weird, beautiful, and completely unforgettable.

picks.t: RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me
picks.d: BTS's RM brings 200 works from his personal collection to Floor 7 at SFMOMA, including many Korean artworks never before shown in the US alongside pieces from the museum's own holdings. Whether you're a fan or just a curious art lover, this one is worth going out of your way for.

Over 50 free experiences take over Market Street for one night only — performances, art installations, and theater spilling out onto SF's main drag. A small handful of shows are ticketed but the vast majority is totally free and no RSVP required. Perfect for wandering with a friend on a Saturday night.

picks.t: Sundown Cinema — Beetlejuice at Crane Cove Park
picks.d: The SF Standard presents an outdoor screening of Beetlejuice at Crane Cove Park — free, spooky-season-appropriate, and right on the waterfront. Bring a blanket, grab some snacks, and settle in for one of the most fun free Friday evenings you can have in this city.

picks.t: Nice As Fuck — Back As F**k Nice As Ever (10th Anniversary Tour)
picks.d: Jenny Lewis, Erika Spring, and Tennessee Thomas reunite as Nice As Fuck for a rare 10th anniversary tour with a reissued album and DJ Alix Brown in tow. August Hall is a great room and this is one of the most charming, feel-good indie-pop shows of the season.

Cole Escola's Tony-winning dark comedy is on its national tour and playing the Curran through November 1st. Wickedly funny, totally unhinged in the best possible way, and already a modern comedy classic — if you haven't grabbed tickets yet, this week is your window.

ongoing.t: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young Museum
ongoing.d: Stunning Egyptian exhibition open Tue–Sun through January 31, 2027.

ongoing.t: Ha Chong-Hyun: Retrospective — Asian Art Museum
ongoing.d: Major Korean painter retrospective through January 25, 2027.

ongoing.t: Mountains of the Mind — Asian Art Museum
ongoing.d: Chinese landscape exhibition closing soon — through October 26 only.
The 7 Fingers' acrobatic love letter to SF, ongoing in North Beach.

ongoing.t: Peter Pan Goes Wrong — SF Playhouse
ongoing.d: Bay Area premiere of the hit comedy, running through November 28.
SF's beloved literary festival runs citywide through October 24, many events free.

new.name: Bayview Oyster Bar
new.d: New Orleans-style raw and grilled oysters, clam chowder, and Dungeness crab with garlic noodles from the chef behind the beloved Auntie April's.

new.name: Rose Pizzeria
new.d: The NYT-acclaimed Berkeley original finally has an SF outpost — currently on the Chronicle's Now List and worth every bit of the hype.

new.name: Fù Huì Huá
new.d: Hot new entry on Resy's October Hit List, part of SF's exciting wave of acclaimed Chinese fine-dining openings.

new.name: Ah Ma's Kitchen
new.d: Cantonese flavors and Hong Kong soul on Clement Street — cracked Yelp's national Best New Restaurants of 2026 list.

new.name: La Kalidad
new.d: First brick-and-mortar for this farmers market darling — calamansi blueberry cruffins and pineapple pulled pork croissants are the move.

classic.name: Bar Shoji
classic.d: Freshly opened Japanese-inspired cocktail bar in SoMa — sleek, precise, and already a neighborhood go-to.

classic.name: Sutro Hall
classic.d: Watch this space: the stunning former Mourad dining room becomes a California-Mediterranean grill this November.

bars.name: Bar Shoji
bars.d: The hottest new bar in SoMa — Japanese-inspired cocktails in a sleek, intimate setting perfect for a Friday night.

bars.name: Public Works
bars.d: 16-year anniversary weekend with Carl Craig and Moodymann Friday, QUEEN OUT x FAKE & GAY Saturday — the place to be this week.

bars.name: 1015 Folsom
bars.d: SF's legendary 1,400-capacity dance institution hosts NOMADZ X DARNA on Friday and X CLUB. on Thursday.

bars.name: The Great Northern
bars.d: Lee Foss on Saturday and a two-night queer dance party — one of SF's best rooms for proper electronic music.

bars.name: Audio SF
bars.d: Regard on Friday, Welker on Saturday, David Harness and DJ Spen on Sunday — a full weekend of great DJ bookings.

bars.name: DACHA Kitchen & Bar
bars.d: Hosts the Black & Dating singles mixer Thursday and is a genuinely lovely neighborhood bar in its own right.

bars.name: O'Reilly's Pub
bars.d: Beloved Haight Ashbury Irish pub — speed dating on Sunday but honestly a great low-key drink any night of the week.

bars.name: The Midway
bars.d: Yheti brings bass and psychedelic electronic vibes on Saturday night to one of SF's largest and most versatile club spaces.

games.detail: NBA Preseason — get a look at the Dubs before the regular season tips off Oct 23
Rare behind-the-scenes look at the team — limited tickets, great value

games.teams: Valkyries vs. Atlanta Dream — WNBA Finals Game 1
games.detail: First Finals appearance in franchise history — this is history, be there

games.teams: Valkyries vs. Atlanta Dream — WNBA Finals Game 2
games.detail: Home court advantage game — the Chase Center will be electric

sports.note: Both games at Chase Center — expect sellout crowds, buy early

concerts.d: The British pop star's biggest tour to date hits The Warfield with DHRUV opening. Presented by Goldenvoice, this is a slick, gorgeous evening of sophisticated disco-pop from one of the UK's finest. Already sold out — check resale immediately.

SF metal legends return home after eight years for two landmark nights at the Fillmore behind their new album. Aaron Turner guests. Friday has Kowloon Walled City. An absolute must for anyone who takes heavy music seriously.

concerts.t: Sara Bareilles — The Good Grief Tour
concerts.d: Her first album in seven years, Good Grief, arrives August 28th and this tour is already selling out theaters across the country. Celisse opens both nights. Warm, intimate, and genuinely moving — one of the best live performers in pop.
concerts.venue: Bill Graham Civic Auditorium · Check Ticketmaster

concerts.d: The Australian indie-rock quartet brings their sun-drenched hooks and anthemic energy to one of SF's most beautiful small rooms. GAMH's ornate hall was basically built for this kind of show.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check GAMH

concerts.d: Boundary-obliterating Canadian provocateur Peaches does her thing at GAMH with SOLTERA, Sola Guinto, and Shifters!! in tow. Expect theatrical mayhem, killer beats, and a room full of people who showed up ready for anything.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall · Check GAMH

concerts.d: Jenny Lewis, Erika Spring, and Tennessee Thomas celebrate a decade of their beloved self-titled record with a rare West Coast stop and DJ Alix Brown. Sweet, fun, and totally worth your Sunday night.
Jakob Dylan's enduring alt-rock band plays the Fillmore — one of the most intimate and storied stages in rock. One Headlight will sound incredible in that room, full stop.

concerts.t: DIIV with Pink Breath of Heaven
concerts.d: New York's premier shoegaze outfit brings their lush, reverb-soaked guitar textures to GAMH on a Wednesday. The perfect mid-week mood reset — hypnotic, immersive, and beautiful.

concerts.t: Imperial Teen, Kids on a Crime Spree & Crows
concerts.d: SF indie-pop institution Imperial Teen headline a stacked triple bill at Bottom of the Hill. Jangly, warm, and locally beloved — this is the best pure local indie night of the week.
concerts.venue: Bottom of the Hill · Check venue

concerts.t: Dom Dolla w/ DJ Seinfeld, HAAi & more
concerts.d: Australian tech-house star Dom Dolla brings one of the biggest electronic lineups of the week to the Cow Palace with DJ Seinfeld, HAAi, Skiis, and Clearcast. A proper large-scale dance music event just south of the city.
concerts.venue: Cow Palace, Daly City · Check ticketing

concertsOngoing.d: Fri–Sun at Davies Symphony Hall, from $51 — joyful, folk-infused, and crowd-pleasing.

concertsOngoing.t: SF Symphony — The Ring (Film with Live Orchestra)
concertsOngoing.d: Tuesday at Davies — perfect spooky season cinema event.
Wednesday Oct 21 at 8pm — rising pop star on a marquee Market Street stage.

concertsOngoing.t: Chelsea Peretti — Back to Work (In Progress) at Punch Line
concertsOngoing.d: Monday Oct 19, 7pm — Brooklyn Nine-Nine star workshopping fresh material in an intimate club.

concertsOngoing.t: Laurie Kilmartin at Punch Line SF
concertsOngoing.d: Wednesday Oct 21, 8pm — sharp, darkly funny storytelling at SF's longest-running comedy club.

concertsOngoing.t: Heavens to Betsy at Bottom of the Hill
concertsOngoing.d: Sat–Sun, both nights sold out — check resale for Corin Tucker's riot grrrl duo.

singles.d: A costume-friendly Halloween singles mixer in SoMa with drink specials, name tags, and built-in icebreakers. Low stakes, high fun — showing up in a good costume instantly gives you something to talk about with literally everyone there.

More than speed dating — this is a structured experience designed to create real chemistry beyond small talk. Hosted by The Tantra Institute in a yoga studio setting, it's the right vibe for open-minded singles who are tired of apps and surface-level connections.

Classic format, fun crowd, Broadway bar vibes — this is speed dating done the easy, unpretentious way. Paris 75 is a perfect SF bar for meeting strangers and the format means you'll talk to a lot of people in two hours.

Sunday evening speed dating at O'Reilly's Pub in Haight Ashbury — relaxed format, neighborhood pub setting, and a targeted age range so you're actually meeting people in your orbit. A great way to ease into the week with a light social adventure.

singles.t: Black & Dating — Mixer at DACHA Kitchen & Bar
singles.d: A Black-centered but open-to-all singles mixer at DACHA in Lower Nob Hill — warm, intentional, and a genuinely nice alternative to the usual chaotic bar scene. Great spot, great vibe, easy to actually have a real conversation.

singlesOngoing.t: Slow Runners Club — Sunday Morning Run
singlesOngoing.d: Every Sunday 10am at the Panhandle — 2,300+ members, all paces welcome, coffee after.
Tuesday evenings in GGP, Thursday Kezar speedwork, Saturday adventure runs — social club first, running club second.
Basketball, soccer, kickball, pickleball and more — weekly games, built-in teammates, genuinely fun community.

date.title: Beetlejuice & a Waterfront Walk
date.tagline: Spooky season romance, zero dollars spent

steps.title: Crane Cove Park Arrival
steps.detail: Get there early for Sundown Cinema's free Beetlejuice screening — grab a good blanket spot before it fills up. Bring snacks and something warm.

steps.title: Beetlejuice Outdoors
steps.detail: Watch the movie under the sky at Crane Cove Park. Classic film, spooky vibes, Dogpatch waterfront — it's genuinely romantic without trying to be.

steps.title: Waterfront Wander
steps.detail: Walk the Dogpatch waterfront after the film. Low pressure, easy conversation, beautiful views. Stop for a drink at a neighborhood spot if the mood is right.

date.title: Sunday Jazz & Oysters
date.tagline: A grown-up Sunday that actually feels special

steps.title: Sunday Streets: Excelsior
steps.detail: Start the day at Sunday Streets in the Excelsior — car-free streets, neighborhood vendors, totally free and a lovely way to wander somewhere new together.

steps.title: Warriors Open Practice
steps.detail: Swing by Chase Center for the Warriors open practice (from ~$6 each). Fun, casual, and a surprisingly great date activity — you'll have plenty to talk about.

steps.title: Bayview Oyster Bar
steps.detail: Head to the new Bayview Oyster Bar on 3rd Street for grilled and raw oysters, garlic noodles, and Dungeness crab. New opening, great energy, genuinely impressive for a date.

date.title: Hisaishi at Davies + Fine Dining
date.tagline: The most magical Thursday night imaginable

steps.title: Pre-Show Dinner at Fù Huì Huá
steps.detail: Lock in a reservation at Fù Huì Huá, October's hottest new Chinese fine-dining spot on the Resy Hit List. Elegant, exciting, and a great way to start a big night.

steps.title: Walk to Davies Symphony Hall
steps.detail: It's a short walk or rideshare to 201 Van Ness. Arrive a few minutes early, grab a drink at the bar, and settle into the gorgeous hall.

steps.title: Joe Hisaishi Conducts Hisaishi
steps.detail: The Studio Ghibli maestro performs his own music live. Expect Totoro, Spirited Away, Princess Mononoke and more — it will absolutely wreck you both in the best possible way. This is the date night of the year.

solo.title: Market Street Night + Litquake
solo.tagline: Art, theater, and books — the ultimate solo SF Saturday

steps.title: Litquake Event
steps.detail: Check the Litquake schedule at litquake.org for free afternoon author readings or panels happening Saturday. A great solo activity — you'll walk away with a book recommendation and maybe a new perspective.

steps.title: Market Street Arts & Theater Festival
steps.detail: The festival runs 4–10pm with 50+ free experiences on Market Street. Solo is actually the perfect way to do this — wander at your own pace, stop for whatever catches your eye, linger as long as you want.

steps.title: Grab a Drink Nearby
steps.detail: You're already on Market Street — pop into a nearby bar, grab a solo drink, and decompress. You earned it.

solo.title: Museum Morning + DIIV Wednesday
solo.tagline: Culture in the afternoon, shoegaze at night

steps.title: Asian Art Museum
steps.detail: Head to the Asian Art Museum for Ha Chong-Hyun's retrospective and — important — Mountains of the Mind closes October 26, so this week is your last real chance. Give yourself two hours.

steps.title: Lunch on Larkin
steps.detail: Grab lunch near the Asian Art Museum in the Civic Center neighborhood before heading home to recharge.

steps.title: DIIV at Great American Music Hall
steps.detail: Head to GAMH for DIIV with Pink Breath of Heaven ($47–50). Shoegaze on a Wednesday in one of SF's most beautiful rooms is the ultimate solo reset — lose yourself in the reverb.

solo.title: Exploratorium After Dark + Late Night Out
solo.tagline: Thursday done right, alone and loving it

steps.title: Early Dinner Solo
steps.detail: Treat yourself to an early dinner at Rose Pizzeria on Clement — the NYT-acclaimed pie is worth it and eating solo at a great pizza place is genuinely one of life's pleasures.

steps.title: Exploratorium After Dark — Día de los Muertos
steps.detail: Head to Pier 15 for After Dark: Death and Life (18+ only, 6–10pm). The whole building becomes a Día de los Muertos experience — weird, beautiful, and absolutely perfect for a solo evening.

steps.title: X CLUB. at 1015 Folsom
steps.detail: You're already in a Thursday night mood — keep it going at 1015 Folsom for X CLUB. Dance as long as you want. You answer to no one.

birthday.title: Golden Gate Park Birthday Day
birthday.tagline: Your city, your park, your day

steps.title: Sunday Streets: Excelsior
steps.detail: If the birthday falls on Sunday, kick things off at Sunday Streets in the Excelsior — car-free, festive, and a great way to get the group moving.

steps.title: T-Pain & Ari Lennox Pregame Picnic
steps.detail: Head to Robin Williams Meadow in Golden Gate Park early with a picnic spread before the outdoor concert starts. Stake out a great spot together.

steps.title: T-Pain & Ari Lennox Concert
steps.detail: This is the main event — an outdoor concert with T-Pain headlining and Ari Lennox opening. Incredible birthday energy in one of the world's best settings.

birthday.title: Neurosis Birthday Pilgrimage
birthday.tagline: For the birthday person who knows what they love

steps.title: Pre-Show Dinner
steps.detail: Gather the crew for dinner near the Fillmore — the neighborhood has solid options for a group pre-show meal. Make a reservation and give people a place to land.

steps.title: Drinks at a Fillmore Neighborhood Bar
steps.detail: Get the group hyped with a round near the venue before doors. The walk over will build the anticipation perfectly.

steps.title: Neurosis at The Fillmore
steps.detail: SF metal legends playing their home city after eight years — with the birthday crew at the Fillmore. This is a show that will be remembered for a long time.

birthday.title: WNBA Finals + Dinner Birthday Blowout
birthday.tagline: Historic sports + great food = unforgettable birthday

steps.title: Brunch First
steps.detail: Start the birthday at Ah Ma's Kitchen on Clement — Hong Kong soul food that Yelp just named one of the best new restaurants in the country. Weekend brunch with your people is the right way to open a big day.

steps.title: Head to Chase Center
steps.detail: WNBA Finals Game 1 tips off at 12:30pm on Saturday. Get there early, soak in the atmosphere, and be part of a genuinely historic moment for Bay Area sports.

steps.title: Post-Game Celebration Dinner
steps.detail: After the game, take the crew to Fù Huì Huá or another splurge-worthy dinner spot to close out the birthday properly. Tickets, food, history — that's a birthday.

friends.title: Free Saturday Adventure
friends.tagline: Three free things, one great Saturday

steps.title: Potrero Hill R&B Festival
steps.detail: SF's 51st Annual Potrero Hill R&B Festival runs 10am–5pm on 20th Street between Wisconsin and Missouri. Free live music, neighborhood vibes, and the whole day ahead of you.

steps.title: Bay Area Science Festival
steps.detail: Swing by UCSF Mission Bay for 125+ free hands-on science experiences — it sounds nerdy but it's genuinely fun for any group of adults who are willing to be a little curious.

steps.title: Market Street Arts & Theater Festival
steps.detail: Close the day on Market Street with 50+ free performances and installations running until 10pm. Walk, wander, grab a drink, and let the city entertain you.

friends.title: Bearrison + Peaches Saturday
friends.tagline: SF at its most gloriously itself

steps.title: Bearrison Street Fair
steps.detail: The Sisters of Perpetual Indulgence's annual Harrison Street fair runs noon–6pm near 11th Street. Free to enter, full of music, dancing, and characters. This is pure SF.

steps.title: Late Lunch at Rose Pizzeria
steps.detail: The NYT-acclaimed Inner Richmond pizzeria is a great mid-afternoon group meal. Order a few pies, catch up, and take your time before the night kicks off.

steps.title: Peaches at Great American Music Hall
steps.detail: Doors at 5pm for Peaches at GAMH as part of Psyched! Fest. A boundary-pushing, theatrical, and completely unhinged live show — perfect for a friend group that's ready for anything.

friends.title: WNBA Finals Friends Day
friends.tagline: Historic hoops + a proper night out

steps.title: Pre-Game Brunch
steps.detail: Meet at Ah Ma's Kitchen or La Kalidad for a festive pre-game brunch. Get the group together, order a lot of food, and get everyone hyped.

steps.title: Valkyries vs. Dream — WNBA Finals Game 1
steps.detail: Chase Center for the first-ever WNBA Finals game for the Golden State Valkyries. The energy will be unlike anything you've experienced at a sporting event in SF in years.

steps.title: Post-Game at Public Works Pre-Party
steps.detail: Ride the high from the game straight into the Public Works 16-year anniversary kickoff night with Carl Craig and Moodymann. Sports to techno: the perfect SF Saturday arc.

parents.title: Museum & Park Day
parents.tagline: Show them the SF that never gets old

steps.title: Sunday Streets: Excelsior
steps.detail: Start Sunday morning at the car-free Excelsior Sunday Streets — easy walking, neighborhood character, and a relaxed pace that's perfect for parents who want to see a real SF neighborhood.

steps.title: Lunch at Ah Ma's Kitchen
steps.detail: Take them to Ah Ma's Kitchen on Clement Street for Hong Kong-style Cantonese food that just made a national best-of list. Clement Street is also a great neighborhood to wander after lunch.

steps.title: de Young Museum — Treasures of the Pharaohs
steps.detail: The de Young's Egyptian exhibition is a genuinely impressive show that parents will love. Golden Gate Park, great art, and an easy afternoon with no loud music required.

parents.title: Dvořák & Dinner
parents.tagline: A proper cultural evening, SF style

steps.title: Dinner Near Davies
steps.detail: Reserve a table near Davies Symphony Hall for an early dinner before the concert. The Van Ness corridor has solid options — keep it classic and unhurried.

steps.title: Walk to Davies Symphony Hall
steps.detail: A short walk to 201 Van Ness. Grab a drink at the lobby bar and let them soak in the beautiful hall before the concert.

steps.title: SF Symphony — Dvořák Symphony No. 8
steps.detail: One of the most joyful and accessible works in the orchestral canon, performed by the SF Symphony. Running Friday, Saturday, and Sunday — a universally pleasing, genuinely lovely evening from $51.

parents.title: Hisaishi + SF's Best New Restaurant
parents.tagline: The kind of visit they'll talk about for years

steps.title: Fù Huì Huá for Dinner
steps.detail: Take them to one of SF's most talked-about new openings for a celebratory meal. Elegant Chinese fine dining that's sophisticated without being stuffy — impressive in the best way.

steps.title: Travel to Davies Symphony Hall
steps.detail: It's a short rideshare to 201 Van Ness. Arrive relaxed, get settled, and enjoy the pre-concert atmosphere in one of SF's grandest venues.

steps.title: Joe Hisaishi Conducts Hisaishi
steps.detail: The composer of My Neighbor Totoro, Spirited Away, and Princess Mononoke conducts his own music live. Whether your parents know Ghibli or not, the music will move them — guaranteed. This is the show of the year.
